headline: Felwine Sarr, writer: 'African Nations' budgets could be directed toward dignity'
description: In a new essay, the Senegalese writer explores what might foster the emergence of African societies more focused on individual dignity. In an interview with Le Monde, he argues that public policies must be rethought and redefined around local philosophies and resources.

headline: Alain Robert, the 'French Spiderman': 'Falling is not an option'
description: In an interview with Le Monde, climber Alain Robert reflects on the sensation that drives him to risk his life by scaling the world's tallest skyscrapers without any ropes.

headline: Adolf and Rudolf Dassler, the Cain and Abel of sports shoes
description: 'Sewn and torn' (6/6). Love stories and friendships can sometimes end badly, even in the world of fashion. United by their passion for sports, the two German brothers grew their shoe factory for more than a decade. Separated by WWII, each went on to create his own brand, Adidas and Puma, through which their fierce rivalry was played out.

headline: 'The End of Oak Street': Jurassic Park comes to suburban America
description: Blending prehistoric science fiction with a satire of American suburbia, David Robert Mitchell playfully subverts the conventions of Steven Spielberg's blockbuster, delivering a B-movie that is both wild and cleverly twisted.

headline: 'We are losing our youth': In northern Morocco, mourning those who drowned off Ceuta
description: In Tétouan, families mourn the deaths of many young men who tried to swim to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta at the end of July. According to a Moroccan non-profit organization, over 140 people lost their lives. Despite these tragedies, many still dream of reaching Europe clandestinely.

headline: Mortality during heatwaves: Key housing, inequality and hospital factors remain overlooked
description: The French government has focused its heatwave messaging on individual actions, preventative measures, and vigilance, but failed to emphasize several central issues that are vital to tackling the heat's most severe health impacts.
